core_obligations: Reduce to a separable algebra (proof lines 3598-3612): decompose the finite algebra into local Artinian factors and let the target be the product of those residue fields which are separable over the base field; every given algebra map factors through that quotient, so one may replace the algebra by it and assume the algebra is finite separable.

Base change to an algebraic closure (proof lines 3612-3625): the traces are compatible with extending the coefficient field, so one may assume the base field algebraically closed, in which case the algebra and all the finite separable algebras involved are products of copies of the field.

Conclude by minimal idempotents (proof lines 3625-3653): under a surjection a minimal idempotent maps to a minimal idempotent or to zero; if the two surjections differ, a minimal idempotent maps to zero under one and to a minimal idempotent under the other, so the two traces take the values zero and one; on the other hand the trace of the image of an idempotent under any of the maps is an integer, so the assumed relation would express plus or minus one as a multiple by an integer larger than one, which is impossible.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the algebra and reduce to a finite separable algebra.
Extend scalars to an algebraic closure.
Use minimal idempotents and integrality of traces to derive a contradiction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a nontrivial integer multiple of a sum of traces of algebra maps equals the difference of the traces of two surjective algebra maps, then the two surjections coincide (statement lines 3590-3603). The proof (proof lines 3604-3653) reduces to a finite separable algebra, extends scalars to an algebraic closure, and uses minimal idempotents together with the integrality of traces on idempotents. H3: a three stage reduction with an explicit contradiction, written out in full.
